item.title: Weight-Bearing Ankle Dorsiflexion MWM
clinicalUse: Limited weight-bearing dorsiflexion after healed ankle injury
patientPosition: Standing lunge position with foot flat and support available.
therapistPosition: In front/side of ankle using belt/manual contact.
stabilization: Foot remains flat; tibia moves forward in line with second toe.
contact: Belt/manual contact provides posterior talar glide while tibia advances.
forceDirection: Sustained posterior talar glide during active dorsiflexion lunge.
item.visualCue: Posterior talar glide + forward tibial lunge → Heel stays down.

subTechniques.name: Weight-Bearing Ankle MWM
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve limited weight-bearing dorsiflexion when a sustained glide produces an immediate increase in lunge range.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Half-kneeling or standing lunge with the heel fully down and foot pointing forward.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the foot. Use a belt/manual contact to sustain an anterior tibial glide or posterior talar correction according to the trained setup.
subTechniques.direction: Maintain the glide while the patient actively drives the knee forward over the foot without heel lift.
subTechniques.reassess: Weight-bearing lunge distance, squat depth and gait.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: If the heel lifts or the arch collapses, the apparent dorsiflexion gain may be compensation.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid in acute unstable ankle injury or fracture.
